summary: Everyone must come to the Beis HaMikdash on the three Yamim Tovim to "be seen" there with a korban, except some people the mishnah lists. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about which small child must come.

chunks.en: Everyone must come to be seen in the Beis HaMikdash on Yom Tov,
chunks.explain: This mitzvah is called re'iyah, being seen.
chunks.st: All are obligated on the three pilgrim Festivals in the mitzva of appearance, i.e., to appear in the Temple as well as to sacrifice an offering,

words.note: The mitzvah to come to the Beis HaMikdash on Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos and bring a korban.

chunks.en: except a person who cannot hear or speak,
chunks.st: except for a deaf-mute,

words.note: A person who cannot hear or speak.

chunks.en: a person whose mind is not well, and a small child,
chunks.st: an imbecile, and a minor;

words.note: A person whose mind does not work properly.
A child who is not yet bar mitzvah.

chunks.en: a tumtum and an androginos,
chunks.st: and a tumtum, and a hermaphrodite,

words.note: A person whom we cannot tell is a boy or a girl.
A person who seems to be both a boy and a girl.

chunks.en: women, and slaves who were not set free,
chunks.st: and women, and slaves who are not emancipated;

chunks.en: someone who cannot walk well, and a blind person,
chunks.st: and the lame, and the blind,

chunks.en: a sick person, and an old person,
chunks.st: and the sick, and the old,

chunks.en: and anyone who cannot go up to Yerushalayim on his own feet.
chunks.st: and one who is unable to ascend to Jerusalem on his own legs.

chunks.en: Which child counts as "a small child" who does not have to come?
chunks.st: Who has the status of a minor with regard to this halakha?

chunks.he: כֹּל שֶׁאֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִרְכּוֹב עַל כְּתֵפָיו
chunks.en: Any child who cannot ride on the shoulders
chunks.st: Any child who is unable to ride on his father’s shoulders

chunks.he: שֶׁל אָבִיו וְלַעֲלוֹת מִירוּשָׁלַיִם לְהַר הַבַּיִת,
chunks.en: of his father and go up from Yerushalayim to Har HaBayis.
chunks.st: and ascend from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount;

words.note: Har HaBayis is the mountain where the Beis HaMikdash stood.

chunks.en: That is what Beis Shammai say.
chunks.st: this is the statement of Beit Shammai.

words.note: Beis Shammai are the students of Shammai.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

words.note: Beis Hillel are the students of Hillel.

chunks.en: Any child who cannot hold
chunks.st: Any child who is unable to hold

chunks.en: his father's hand
chunks.st: his father’s hand

chunks.en: and walk up from Yerushalayim to Har HaBayis.
chunks.st: and ascend on foot from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount,

chunks.en: Because the Torah says "three regalim."
chunks.explain: Regel also means foot: you go up on your feet.
chunks.st: as it is stated: “Three times [regalim]” (Exodus 23:14).
chunks.stMore: Since the term for feet is raglayim, Beit Hillel infer from here that the obligation to ascend involves the use of one’s legs.

words.note: Times, or Yamim Tovim; the word sounds like raglayim, feet.

summary: How much money must be spent on the re'iyah korban and the chagigah korban? Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: The re'iyah korban must cost at least two silver coins,
chunks.st: The burnt-offering of appearance brought on a pilgrim Festival must be worth at least two silver coins,

words.note: An olah korban brought when coming to be seen in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: and the chagigah korban at least one silver ma'ah.
chunks.st: and the Festival peace-offering must be worth at least one silver ma’a coin.

words.note: A shelamim korban brought for the Yom Tov and eaten in celebration.
A small silver coin.

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: The re'iyah korban must cost at least one silver ma'ah,
chunks.st: The burnt-offering of appearance must be worth at least one silver ma’a

chunks.en: and the chagigah korban at least two silver coins.
chunks.st: and the Festival peace-offering at least two silver coins.

summary: Which money may be used to buy the Yom Tov korbanos? Olos must be bought with regular money, but shelamim may be bought with maaser sheni money.

chunks.en: Olos brought on Yom Tov must be bought with regular money,
chunks.explain: Not with maaser sheni money, which is holy.
chunks.st: Burnt-offerings that one sacrifices on the intermediate days of the Festival must come from non-sacred property,
chunks.stMore: not from sacred property such as second-tithe money.

words.note: Korbanos that are burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: but the shelamim may come from maaser money.
chunks.st: But the peace-offerings may be brought from the second tithe,
chunks.stMore: i.e., from money with which one redeemed second tithe, which is subsequently used to purchase food in Jerusalem.

words.note: Korbanos that are mostly eaten by the people who bring them.
Maaser sheni: money used to buy food to eat in Yerushalayim.

chunks.en: About the chagigah of the first day of Pesach,
chunks.st: With regard to the Festival peace-offering sacrificed on the first day of the festival of Passover,

words.note: Yom Tov means a holiday.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say:
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: it must come from regular money.
chunks.st: It must come from non-sacred property,

chunks.en: And Beis Hillel say:
chunks.st: and Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: It may come from maaser money.
chunks.st: It may be brought even from the second tithe.

summary: On Yom Tov there is a mitzvah to be happy by eating meat of korbanos. This mishnah teaches which korbanos count for this mitzvah.

chunks.en: Regular Jews do their mitzvah of being happy on Yom Tov
chunks.st: In general, Israelites fulfill their obligation to eat peace-offerings of rejoicing

words.note: Jews who are not Kohanim.

chunks.en: with korbanos they promised to bring, and with maaser animals.
chunks.st: with their voluntary vows and gift offerings donated during the year and sacrificed on the Festival; and likewise with animal tithes.

words.note: Every tenth animal born was brought as a korban.

chunks.en: And the Kohanim do it with chatas and asham korbanos,
chunks.st: And the priests fulfill their obligation of rejoicing with the meat of sin-offerings and guilt-offerings

words.note: Korbanos brought for some sins; the Kohanim eat them.
Another kind of korban for a sin; the Kohanim eat them.

chunks.en: with the bechor, and with the chest and leg they get from shelamim.
chunks.st: and with firstborn offerings, as the priests receive a portion of these, and with the breast and thigh of peace-offerings, to which they are also entitled.

words.note: A firstborn animal, given to the Kohanim.

chunks.en: But not with birds and not with flour korbanos.
chunks.explain: Only eating meat counts as being happy.
chunks.st: However, they do not fulfill their obligation with birds, e.g., a bird sacrificed as a sin-offering, nor with meal-offerings,
chunks.stMore: as only the eating of meat constitutes rejoicing.

words.note: Korbanos made of flour.

summary: A person with a big family should bring more shelamim to feed them, and a rich person with a small family should bring more olos. A person who has a lot should give a lot.

chunks.en: Someone who has many people to feed
chunks.st: One who has many eaters, i.e., members of his household,

chunks.en: and only a little money
chunks.st: and a small amount of property,

chunks.en: brings many shelamim and few olos.
chunks.explain: He can feed his family from the shelamim.
chunks.st: may bring many peace-offerings and few burnt-offerings,
chunks.stMore: so he can feed the members of his household with the peace-offerings.

chunks.en: If he has lots of money and few people to feed,
chunks.st: If one has much property and few eaters,

chunks.en: he brings many olos and few shelamim.
chunks.st: he should bring many burnt-offerings and few peace-offerings.

chunks.en: If he has little of both,
chunks.st: If both these and those, his property and the members of his household, are few,

chunks.en: about him the Rabbis said
chunks.st: with regard to this individual it is stated in the mishna (2a)

chunks.en: one silver ma'ah and two silver coins.
chunks.explain: The smallest amounts taught in the mishnah before.
chunks.st: that the Sages established the smallest amount of one silver ma’a for the burnt-offering of appearance in the Temple and two silver coins for the Festival peace-offerings.

chunks.en: If he has a lot of both,
chunks.st: If both his eaters and his property are many,

chunks.en: about him the Torah says:
chunks.st: with regard to this individual it is stated:

chunks.en: "Each man as he can give, like the bracha of Hashem
chunks.st: “Every man shall give as he is able, according to the blessing of the Lord

chunks.en: your G-d which He gave you."
chunks.st: your God, which He has given you” (Deuteronomy 16:17).

summary: If someone did not bring his chagigah korban on the first day of Yom Tov, he can still bring it later in the Yom Tov. Once Yom Tov is over, he can no longer make it up.

chunks.en: Someone who did not bring his chagigah korban
chunks.st: With regard to one who did not celebrate by bringing the Festival peace-offering

chunks.en: on the first day of Sukkos,
chunks.st: on the first day of the festival of Sukkot,

words.note: Sukkos.

chunks.en: may bring it all the rest of the Yom Tov
chunks.st: he may celebrate and bring it during the entire remaining days of the pilgrimage Festival,

words.note: The Yom Tov.

chunks.en: and even on the last day, Shemini Atzeres.
chunks.st: and even on the final day of the Festival, i.e., on the Eighth Day of Assembly.

chunks.en: If the Yom Tov passed and he did not bring it,
chunks.st: If the pilgrimage Festival passed and one did not celebrate by bringing the Festival peace-offering,

chunks.en: he does not have to make it up.
chunks.explain: It is too late; the chance for the mitzvah is gone.
chunks.st: he is not obligated to pay restitution for it.
chunks.stMore: Even if he consecrated an animal for this purpose and it was lost, once the Festival is over he has no obligation to replace it, as he has missed the opportunity for performing this mitzva.

chunks.en: About this the pasuk says:
chunks.st: And about this it is stated:

chunks.en: "Something crooked cannot be made straight,
chunks.st: “That which is crooked cannot be made straight;

chunks.en: and something missing cannot be counted."
chunks.st: and that which is wanting cannot be numbered” (Ecclesiastes 1:15).

summary: Two Rabbis explain the pasuk "something crooked cannot be made straight." Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says it means a talmid chacham who stops learning Torah.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya says:

chunks.en: What is the crooked thing that cannot be fixed?
chunks.st: Who is the crooked that cannot be made straight?

chunks.en: This is someone who did a forbidden relationship
chunks.st: This verse is referring to one who engaged in intercourse with a woman forbidden to him

chunks.en: and a mamzer was born from it.
chunks.explain: A mamzer's status can never be changed.
chunks.st: and fathered a mamzer with her.
chunks.stMore: This individual is unable to rectify his sin, because the status of the illegitimate child is permanent.

words.note: A child born from a forbidden relationship; his status stays forever.

chunks.en: If you say it means someone who steals or robs,
chunks.st: And if you say that it is referring to one who steals or robs,

chunks.en: he can give it back and fix what he did.
chunks.st: although he is crooked he can return what he stole and in this manner his sin will be rectified.

chunks.en: Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai says:
chunks.st: Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai says:

chunks.en: We call something crooked only if
chunks.st: One calls crooked only someone

chunks.en: it was straight at first and then became crooked.
chunks.st: who was initially straight and subsequently became crooked.

chunks.he: וְאֵיזֶה, זֶה תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הַפּוֹרֵשׁ מִן הַתּוֹרָה:
chunks.en: And who is this? A talmid chacham who leaves the Torah.
chunks.st: And who is this? This is a Torah scholar who leaves his Torah study.
chunks.stMore: Here is an example of something straight that became crooked.

words.note: A talmid chacham is a Torah scholar.

summary: Some parts of Torah have only a tiny hint in the pasukim but many halachos, and some have a strong source in the Torah. The ones with a strong source are the main parts of the Torah.
stIntro: Incidental to the Festival peace-offering, the mishna describes the nature of various areas of Torah study.

chunks.en: The halachos of undoing a neder fly in the air,
chunks.st: The halakhot of the dissolution of vows, when one requests from a Sage to dissolve them, fly in the air

words.note: Promises a person makes, which a Rav can undo.

chunks.en: and have almost nothing in the Torah to lean on.
chunks.explain: The Torah only hints at them.
chunks.st: and have nothing to support them,
chunks.stMore: as these halakhot are not mentioned explicitly in the Torah. There is only a slight allusion to the dissolution of vows in the Torah, which is taught by the Sages as part of the oral tradition.

chunks.en: The halachos of Shabbos,
chunks.st: The halakhot of Shabbat,

chunks.en: chagigah korbanos, and me'ilah,
chunks.st: Festival peace-offerings, and misuse of consecrated property

words.note: Me'ilah is using something that belongs to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: are like mountains hanging by a hair,
chunks.st: are like mountains suspended by a hair,

chunks.en: because they have few pesukim and many halachos.
chunks.st: as they have little written about them in the Torah, and yet the details of their halakhot are numerous.

chunks.en: The laws of judging and the avodah in the Beis HaMikdash,
chunks.st: The details of monetary law, sacrificial rites,

words.note: Laws a beis din judges, like money cases.
The service in the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: tahara, tumah, and forbidden relationships,
chunks.st: ritual purity and impurity, and the halakhot of those with whom relations are forbidden

words.note: Relatives a person may not marry.

chunks.en: have something in the Torah to lean on.
chunks.st: all have something to support them, i.e., there is ample basis in the Torah for these halakhot,

chunks.en: They are the main parts of the Torah.
chunks.st: and these are the essential parts of Torah.
